newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Nauru parliament elects new preisdent.
newsitem.headline: Nauru parliament elects new preisdent.

text.p: The Republic of Nauru announced on Tuesday that its former justice minister Bernard Dowiyogo had been elected as the South Pacific nation's new president after a vote of no confidence in the previous government.
"There's just been a reshuffle in the parliament," Nauru's Melbourne-based public affairs consultant Helen Bogdan told Reuters.
"There was a vote of no-confidence in the previous government and Dowiyogo is forming a (new) cabinet," she said.
Dowiyogo, 50, was re-elected after 12 months away from the position, replacing Lagumot Harris who has presided over the Pacific island's 18-member parliament since November 19 last year.
Twelve members of parliament disgruntled with the economic management of Nauru by its previous cabinet signed a no-confidence motion last Thursday, sparking the reshuffle, Bogdan said.
"They were unhappy about the economic running of the country," she said.
On Monday eight members of parliament voted for Dowiyogo and seven against, while two members and the Speaker abstained, Bodgan said.
Dowiyogo first became president in 1976, taking power from the country's founding leader Sir Hammer de Roburt, who returned to power in 1978.
Dowiyogo won the presidency for the second time in 1989 and subsequently in 1992 and 1993.
Nauru, a small island of 8,000 people about 2,400 miles (3,900 km) northeast of Australia, has only one natural resource -- high-grade phosphate that is used in fertilisers.
Former president Harris last month agreed to consider an offer by The Philippines to sell its stake in a loss-making joint venture fertiliser company to Nauru, its equal partner in the venture.
